tasks.title: The Closeable protocol
tasks.statement: Write a Protocol Closeable with a method close() (with the runtime_checkable decorator) and a function close_all(items): it closes everything that matches the protocol and returns how many objects were closed. Skip the others.
tasks.hint: @runtime_checkable class Closeable(Protocol): def close(self) -> None: ...; in close_all: if isinstance(item, Closeable): item.close().

tasks.title: A protocol with an attribute
tasks.statement: Write a runtime_checkable protocol HasName with an attribute name: str and a function names(items): a list of the name values of the objects that match the protocol (the others are skipped).
tasks.hint: class HasName(Protocol): name: str - and @runtime_checkable; in names: [x.name for x in items if isinstance(x, HasName)].

tasks.title: A generic stack
tasks.statement: Write a generic Stack(Generic[T]) with methods push(x), pop() (IndexError on an empty stack), peek() and __len__. The form Stack[int]() must also create a working stack.
tasks.hint: class Stack(Generic[T]) with a list inside; pop() on an empty list already raises IndexError.

tasks.title: Box in the new syntax
tasks.statement: Write a class Box[T] using the new type parameter syntax (Python 3.12+, without Generic and TypeVar): a field value, a method map(f) that returns a new Box holding f(value), and a __repr__ of the form Box(3).
tasks.hint: class Box[T]: def __init__(self, value: T): ...; def map[U](self, f) -> "Box[U]": return Box(f(self.value)).

tasks.title: TypeVar with a bound
tasks.statement: Define a protocol Comparable (method __lt__(self, other) -> bool), a type variable T = TypeVar("T", bound=Comparable) and a function biggest(items: list[T]) -> T that returns the largest element.
tasks.hint: class Comparable(Protocol): def __lt__(self, other) -> bool: ...; T = TypeVar("T", bound=Comparable).

tasks.title: Overloading for the type checker
tasks.statement: Define a function first with two @overload stubs (str → str and list[int] → int) and one real implementation that returns the first element. typing.get_overloads(first) must see the two stubs.
tasks.hint: @overload def first(x: str) -> str: ...; @overload def first(x: list[int]) -> int: ...; then def first(x): return x[0].

tasks.title: Method chains with Self
tasks.statement: Write a class Query with methods where(cond) and limit(n): both store the settings in the instance, return self, and are annotated with the result typing.Self (so that subclasses keep their own type). The method build() returns a string like «WHERE a AND b LIMIT 3».
tasks.hint: build: parts = []; if there are conds - "WHERE " + " AND ".join(conds); if limit is not None - "LIMIT n"; join with a space.

tasks.title: Validating a dict against a TypedDict
tasks.statement: Write validate(data, schema): using the TypedDict hints (typing.get_type_hints(schema)), return a sorted list of errors: "missing key K" (missing key), "extra key K" (extra key), and "K: expected T" (expected T, the type name) if the value has the wrong type.
tasks.hint: hints = typing.get_type_hints(schema); walk over the keys of hints and over the keys of data.

tasks.title: A type in words
tasks.statement: Write describe_type(tp): a string like «list[int]», «dict[str, list[int]]», «int | None» built from an annotation (use typing.get_origin and get_args; for ordinary classes the class name, for NoneType «None», for unions join the parts with « | »).
tasks.hint: origin = typing.get_origin(tp); args = typing.get_args(tp); for Union and UnionType join with " | "; print Ellipsis as «...».
